C001.reason: Request interface unchanged; quantity remains string per input contract.

C002.reason: Must pass int64 directly without JS Number conversion to preserve exact values. parseInt returns Number and violates int64 precision for large values.

C003.reason: entity.quantity.toString() already produces canonical decimal string; int64 toString behavior unchanged.

C004.reason: Must use entity.quantity directly with BigInt constructor instead of Number(entity.quantity) to preserve exact signed int64 values for >0 predicate.

edits.before: const sample = StockItem.encode({ sku: request.sku, quantity: Number.parseInt(request.quantity, 10) }).finish();
edits.after: const sample = StockItem.encode({ sku: request.sku, quantity: BigInt(request.quantity) }).finish();

edits.before: return { fields, in_stock: BigInt(entity.quantity) > 0n, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };
edits.after: return { fields, in_stock: entity.quantity > 0n, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };

rationale: Schema change int32->int64 requires preserving exact quantities. C002: parseInt loses precision; must use BigInt for construction. C004: entity.quantity from ts-proto is already Long (int64); BigInt(entity.quantity) was redundant/wrong; direct comparison with >0n works for Long values in generated bindings.
assumptions: ts-proto generated bindings expose int64 as Long objects supporting > comparison with bigint literals
StockItem.encode accepts Long/ BigInt values for int64 fields
No JS number conversion anywhere in the pipeline to maintain int64 precision
